chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn Suqah, from one who informed him, saying:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to his wife from behind (her rear). He said: 'He is one of the two who have ghusl (ritual bath) upon him.'

key_terms.اَلْمَأْتَيَيْنِ: the two who have intercourse (implying two categories of ghusl)
key_terms.يَأْتِي أَهْلَهُ: comes to his wife (has marital intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ghusl when a husband has intercourse with his wife from behind?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that sexual intercourse from behind necessitates the major ritual bath (*ghusl al-janabah*), placing the husband in the same category as one who ejaculates. This ruling underscores the principle that the act itself, regardless of the position or direction, triggers the state of *janabah* requiring purification, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding marital hygiene and prayer validity.
